rationale: A probe written for the last paused question tripped over a different, sharper client-contract problem: on every node the configuration returned by GetConfiguration had the correct membership while its Index() was 0, even though the caller knew the configuration entry it was reading had index 3. Reading the constructor explains it - the returned future is filled with the latest Configuration only, leaving latestIndex zero - and the guard that consumes such an index is only enforced for non-zero values, so the documented optimistic-concurrency use of the returned index cannot work. The experiment request carries the impact and a control in the same execution.

investigations.question: Does the configuration index exposed by GetConfiguration identify the configuration it returns, and can a caller use that value as the prevIndex guard of a later membership change so that a change is rejected when the configuration has moved on in the meantime?
investigations.hypothesis: GetConfiguration builds its future locally from the atomically published latest configuration and never fills the index field, so ConfigurationFuture.Index() returns the zero value for every caller while Configuration() carries the real membership. The prevIndex guard in nextConfiguration is only enforced when prevIndex is greater than zero, so a caller that passes the returned index is silently unguarded, while the same change guarded with the genuine configuration entry index is rejected once the configuration has advanced.
investigations.discriminator: Read the configuration from the API on each node of a live cluster whose configuration entry index the caller learned from the membership-change future, and compare the returned index with that index; then take an intervening configuration change and retry a guarded change using the value the API returned, with the genuine index as control. A defect needs the returned index not to identify the returned configuration and the guarded change to be applied anyway when the configuration has moved on, while the genuine-index control is rejected; the hypothesis is refuted if the returned index matches the configuration entry index or if the guard rejects the API-derived value.
limitations: Native local run of the requested harness (not retained evidence) showed all four nodes returning index 0 with 4 servers visible and a known configuration entry index of 3, a guarded change using the returned value succeeding, and the genuine-index control failing with 'configuration changed since 3 (latest is 5)'.
The defect is about the value the accessor reports and the guard it feeds; it does not weaken the internal configuration tracking used by the main loop, which is filled through a different path.
No execution receipt exists yet; the controller's execution is what counts.

knowledge.statement: GetConfiguration returns a configurationsFuture whose configurations value is built from the atomically published latest configuration only, so Configuration() reports the real membership while Index() reports the zero value for every caller regardless of the configuration entry the value came from. The membership-change guard in nextConfiguration only enforces prevIndex when it is greater than zero, so an index taken from GetConfiguration cannot express the documented condition that the change applies only to the configuration that was read.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.GetConfiguration on any server and to every membership change command routed through nextConfiguration; the internal configuration tracking filled from the main thread through configurationsCh does carry the index and is unaffected.

scope.description: One fault-free execution on normally bootstrapped in-memory clusters: a 3-node cluster plus one joining voter, a configuration read on every node, an intervening membership change, a guarded change using the index the API returned, and a control change guarded with the genuine configuration entry index.
assumptions: MakeCluster(3) plus MakeClusterNoBootstrap(1) merged and fully connected performs real bootstrap, replication and membership changes through the in-memory transport.
AddVoter's returned future index identifies the configuration entry that the client just created, so it is the independent reference for what the configuration index should report.
The configuration the read is taken against has not changed before the read returns, so the read is the one the caller would guard against.
Between the read and the guarded change the harness performs an intervening membership change, so a correctly guarded change must be rejected.
excluded: Internal configuration tracking used by the main loop, which is obtained through a different path.
Network-transport behaviour and any transport-level effects.
Performance and behaviour of callers that ignore the returned index.

experiment.prefix: Built with captured test facilities and real producers only: MakeCluster(3) bootstraps a three-voter cluster and elects a leader; a second cluster of one node is merged and fully connected, and the leader adds that node with AddVoter, whose future index (3 in the local run) is recorded as the reference configuration index. The harness then emits one config_guard_start admission per node and, for each node, one config_read result carrying the index and membership returned by GetConfiguration plus that reference index. It reads the configuration again, takes an intervening membership change (a further AddVoter, entry 4), then applies a guarded change using the index the API returned, and finally applies a control change guarded with the genuine reference index. No storage is pre-filled and no production code is modified.
experiment.requirement: The configuration index exposed by GetConfiguration identifies the configuration the same call returned, and a membership change guarded with that value is rejected once the configuration has moved on; a change guarded with the genuine configuration entry index is rejected in the same situation.
experiment.responsibility: GetConfiguration's construction of the returned configuration future and nextConfiguration's prevIndex guard, i.e. the client-visible optimistic-concurrency contract for membership changes.

comparisons.description: Every node: the configuration returned by GetConfiguration contains the four servers while its reported index must identify that same configuration, i.e. match the reference index of the configuration entry.
Impact: a change guarded with the index the API returned must be rejected because the configuration moved on after the read; it is applied instead.
Control: the same situation guarded with the genuine configuration entry index is rejected with the configuration-changed error, so the guard itself works when a real index is supplied.
